It needs content. Mobile apps, JSON feeds, transparency, and equality are all nice but at the end of the day sites like Digg, Reddit, and Voat are sites that are driven by content.

Take Reddit, for example, to start out they faked a bunch of users and content to give an idea of business. This kept the front page from being a ghost town. Now, Voats homepage is currently pretty busy, but once all the reddit talk dies down, how much real conversation is going to be left?

Regardless of the other aspects, if Voat is to grow, if any site is to grow, it needs the content required to keep people coming back.

It needs content. Mobile apps, feeds etc are just bells and whistles that are not an essential part of the inherent value of quality content. Once there is content, anyone with a basic level of programming competence can build whatever they want on top of it.
Exclusivity is also important. While may-mays may draw views, the content we provide needs to be unique to this site to maintain readers
